item.title: 🟠 New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
item.description:
Why this matters: Compliance/regulatory signal — determine applicability and required action.
A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access to a locked Windows computer start programs without signing in. Whoever uses it gets only a limited account, not administrator control of the machine. The method was posted yesterday by a researcher who uses the handles MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, and the endpoint-security firm ThreatLocker

Source: The Hacker News  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 6d

item.description:
Why this matters: Service impact is possible — verify vendor status before troubleshooting internally.

item.title: 🟠 phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
item.description:
Why this matters: Useful IT context for operational and leadership awareness.
PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server.
